prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states there, opening the field of moire quantum matter

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B001 alone, with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. After the full first-round exchange the core of the case still stands on the science. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model made a specific, falsifiable statement (flat bands at a magic angle), and experiment found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that condition. The existence of these phases has since been reproduced by independent groups and carried into twisted multilayers and twisted transition-metal dichalcogenides. No member, including the two who prefer B007, argues that the discovery itself is in doubt. The question the committee has to answer is what the citation honours, and I would word it so that it honours the prediction and the observation of the phases, and makes no claim about the pairing mechanism. Written that way, the citation does not depend on the part of the field that is still open. I will vote on that criterion, a tested prediction that opened a new class of systems, and I state it as a judgement about this case and not as a rule that always outranks enabling measurement capability.
statement.case_against: Two reservations remain real and I do not think round 1 removed them. First, credit: Jarillo-Herrero is the only experimental name, and Cao, Fatemi and the Dean, Young, Yazdani and Efetov groups sit outside the three-name limit, as do the earlier twisted-graphene band-structure theorists Olsson and Mehlig mentioned. The group-leader convention is defensible but not comfortable. Second, maturity: the pairing mechanism and several correlated states are unresolved and twist-angle disorder complicates device comparison. If the committee concludes that the lasting content of the discovery is not yet fixed, B007 is the strongest fallback, with a clean two-person attribution and stable interpretation. I would still count the open mechanism against the timing only mildly, because it is a follow-up question and not the discovery.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the lattice clock is a finished capability with stable interpretation and multi-laboratory comparison at the 1e-18 level, whereas twisted graphene is still evolving, and he stresses that the criterion is a change in what can be measured.
responses.response: I accept that B007 is the more settled achievement and that the Katori-Ye attribution is the cleaner one; that is why B007 remains my first alternative and I would not object if the committee ended up there. My answer to the chair's own question about criterion is that in this case the deciding feature is a quantitative prediction tested in nature, which opened a new class of materials, and that is a larger step than extending an existing measurement line to a lower uncertainty. I also note that Kroll's own ranking placed B001 fourth partly because of the open mechanism, yet he has moved it to his first alternative. On his disclosed link to Hall's laboratory, I read that as a point for the record. The link is to a laureate honoured for a different achievement, and the credited pair is Katori and Ye, so I would favour disclosure without recusal, with the committee noting it in the minutes.

responses.point: Lindroth's main reservation about B007 is that a lattice clock builds on the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and that the redefinition of the second is still pending; she also doubts that a citation for B001 can avoid resting on interpretation.
responses.response: Her reservation about B007 is the right one to raise, and I think it is partly answered by her own point that Ye's many-body clock physics and the stability record go beyond the comb work. I would not treat the pending SI redefinition as a condition of maturity. On her doubt about B001, I disagree that the citation rests on interpretation. The citation I propose names the prediction and the observed phases and is silent on the pairing mechanism, so a settled mechanism is not needed for it to be accurate. Where I do agree with her is that this is a choice between two serious configurations and not a case where one is weak, and she should not be asked to accept B001 on the strength of the count of first places alone.

responses.point: Danielsson argues that B001 opens a new class of matter while B007 refines an already honoured field, and that naming Jarillo-Herrero as the one experimental laureate follows the usual group-leader convention.
responses.response: I agree with the first point and I hold it with some care, because a 'new field' argument can be used to favour any fashionable topic. What makes it persuasive here is that the prediction preceded the experiment. On the group-leader convention I am less comfortable than he is. It is a convention, not a proof that the credit is right, and Cao's role as first author is a real fact. I accept it as the least bad option within three names and I will say so openly in the committee record, since the chair's question on this point cannot be fully resolved with the supplied names.

responses.point: Olsson, who moved from B030 to B001, raised earlier twisted-graphene band-structure theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto, Suarez Morell) as bearing on how the citation is worded.
responses.response: I take this seriously as a point about wording and not about the three names. Those earlier calculations found reduced Fermi velocity at small angles, but the continuum model with the specific magic angle and the flat-band condition is the Bistritzer-MacDonald result, and that is what experiment tested. The citation should therefore say prediction of flat bands at a magic angle and not claim that all twisted-graphene theory began there. I also appreciate that she moved from her first-place B030 ranking and that her recusal offer on B030 is unnecessary now that B030 is not in the leading configurations.

uncertainties: Whether three names are enough, given that Cao, Fatemi and other experimental groups, and earlier twisted-graphene theorists, fall outside them.
Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism will be judged by the committee to make B001 premature, and what further evidence would change the views of Kroll and Lindroth.
Whether the committee prefers field-opening novelty or enabling measurement capability; I have stated my criterion for this case but I cannot show that the other criterion is wrong.
For B039, individual credit inside the large IceCube collaboration and whether Spiering belongs among the names remains unresolved, which is why it stays only an alternative.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with B001. As chair I only note that my field proximity to B039 (IceCube), through astroparticle instrumentation, is unchanged: my documented collaborations are PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur, not IceCube, and I identify no recusal issue. On B007, I record Kroll's disclosed Boulder link and Olsson's possible Tokyo link and would treat both as disclosures, not recusals.
